title: EventStream schema negotiation and reconnect semantics for tool-call and structured frames
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our existing SSE implementation treats the stream as a sequence of text chunks. As customers adopt function/tool calling and richer structured outputs (JSON objects with nested fields), simple newline- or chunk-delimited framing causes frequent client-side JSON parse failures during reconnects and when events are split across TCP packets. Additionally, some integrations require multiplexed streams (control + model outputs) and need a graceful compatibility path to older clients that expect bare text/event-stream payloads.

Goal: Define a negotiation handshake, an unambiguous chunk framing schema for structured frames (including tool-call boundaries and metadata), and reconnect semantics that allow clients to resume without duplicating function calls or producing partial structured objects. The implementation must be backward-compatible with existing SSE clients and minimize latency/CPU overhead.

Proposed design: 1) Protocol negotiation: On stream open the server emits a single JSON capability event (event: capabilities) indicating supported framing types, resume token format, and compatibility mode. Clients may opt into "structured-json-v1" framing or remain in "legacy-text" mode. 2) Framing: Structured frames are encoded as length-prefixed UTF-8 JSON records (X-Frame-Length header per event) wrapped into SSE events; each structured event contains: id, seq, type (e.g., "delta", "tool_call_start", "tool_call_chunk", "tool_call_end"), checksum (optional), and payload (base JSON). This balances parseability and stream friendliness. 3) Function/tool-call boundaries: Tool-call sequences are explicitly delimited with start/end events and carry a stable call_id; any intermediate reconnect must rehydrate last-complete-seq and the server will resume streaming remaining chunks for that call_id. 4) Resume tokens: Server issues monotonic resume tokens every N complete logical events (configurable). A resume token encodes: last_seq, call_ids_in_progress (list), and a signature (HMAC) to prevent tampering. Token size is kept small (base64). 5) Reconnect semantics: Clients provide resume token on reconnection. Server validates token and either: a) continues from last_seq (best-effort resume), b) if token expired or invalid, falls back to replay/compact mode where server emits synthesized re-sync events (safe fallbacks) and marks any in-progress tool calls as aborted so clients can re-issue idempotent calls. 6) Backward compatibility: If client does not acknowledge structured-json-v1 in the first exchange, server emits a compatibility shim that flattens structured frames into plain text with embedded markers (e.g., [TOOL_CALL_START id=...]) and keeps a TTL before switching to structured-only mode. 7) Observability and telemetry: Emit metrics for resume success rate, resume latency, truncated-frame errors, and malformed-json raises. Include debug endpoints to decode resume tokens and show outstanding call state per connection.

Trade-offs: - Length-prefixed frames add small overhead but remove ambiguity and simplify resumability. - Resume token HMAC requires key rotation handling; plan lifecycle keys and token invalidation windows. - For extreme low-latency customers we provide an opt-out (legacy-text) where resumability is weaker.

Acceptance criteria: - Server emits capability event on every stream open. - Clients can request structured-json-v1 and receive length-prefixed events that parse deterministically. - Reconnect with valid token resumes within configured window and does not duplicate completed tool calls. - Invalid tokens lead to safe abort semantics and clear re-sync markers. - Backward-compatible clients continue to work unchanged for at least one release cycle.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime-flag and gateway toggle; initial rollout to internal customers and a small beta set, followed by staged enablement across hosted tenants.

Docs & artifacts: design doc, compatibility guide, SDK helpers for resume tokens and client-side rehydration.
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and SDK leads. Agreed on length-prefixed JSON framing over SSE for deterministic parsing.
2026-02-18: PoC server emitted 'capabilities' event; simple client shim in python decoded length-prefixed frames correctly. Linked PoC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proto/pull/76

2026-02-24: Design review with PM (Jared Kim) and Design (Maya Singh). Design feedback: make resume tokens compact and provide human-readable debug endpoint. Action: add HMAC and debug endpoint to plan.
2026-03-02: SDK implementation (node, python, go) prototypes completed. Node SDK added automatic token refresh logic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/182
2026-03-05: Discovered edge-case where tool_call_end emitted before last chunk due to batching. Mitigated by sequence-number enforcement and server-side flush-on-end in default config.
2026-03-09: Security review requested; threat model updated for resume token leakage. Decided on 7-day default token TTL; security action item ENG-119010 to add key-rotation tooling.

2026-03-12: Integration tests added for reconnect scenarios including truncated-json, duplicate-reconnects, and expired-token fallback. All tests passing in CI except one flaky case under high-load; investigating backpressure interactions.
qa_notes: Test reconnect with: 1) client disconnect after partial tool_call_chunk, 2) simultaneous reconnections from same client id, 3) expired token behavior. Validate that no duplicate tool executions are observed in backend logs and that clients receive a clear 'resync' marker when fallback occurs.
migration_notes: Provide SDK-compatible helpers to opt-in to structured-json-v1. Keep compatibility shim enabled for 2 releases. Run migration batch to collect resume-failure telemetry and notify customers via console banner before enforcing structured-only mode.
